heading: Vocabulary of the Language of the Natives of Newfoundland; procured by the Rev. J. Leigh, from Mary March, a Native Woman, taken up the Bay of Exploits by Mr. Peyton, in March, 1818.
short: Vocabulary of the Language of the Natives of Newfoundland
author: H. Robinson (journal); vocabulary by Rev. J. Leigh
collector: Rev. John Leigh, from Mary March (Demasduit)
title: Private Journal kept on board H.M.S. Favorite on the Newfoundland Station. By Captain H. Robinson, R.N. 1820.
imprint: Journal of the Royal Geographical Society of London, 4, 1834, pp. 207-220 (vocabulary pp. 218-220)
about: The Rev. J. Leigh, Church Missionary, took down these words from Mary March, a Native woman of Newfoundland captured up the Bay of Exploits by Mr. Peyton in March 1818, who lived in his house.

heading: I subjoin a short vocabulary of the Carib tongue, which it must be supposed has affinity with some of the languages of Western Africa, from the evident similarity of the Caribs to the negroes of that continent; ... CARIB VOCABULARY.
short: Notice of the Caribs in Central America
author: Juan Galindo
title: Notice of the Caribs in Central America. Communicated by Colonel Don Juan Galindo, F.R.G.S. Dated Government House, Trugillo, 1833.
imprint: Journal of the Royal Geographical Society of London, 3, 1833, pp. 290-291
about: Words of the Caribs of Trugillo, whose people had been moved from St. Vincent to Roatan by the British in 1796 and then to Trugillo by the Spaniards, sent by Galindo from Government House, Trugillo, in 1833.

heading: Dr. Sibley's vocabulary was taken in 1804, when the Caddos were located on Red river, from Alexandria to Natchitoches, and follows the French orthography :
author: Otis T. Mason (section editor); vocabulary by Dr. John Sibley
place: Red River, from Alexandria to Natchitoches, Louisiana
title: Anthropology. Anthropological News
about: A Caddo vocabulary taken in 1804 by Dr. Sibley, agent for the Caddos on the Red River, and sent to Governor Claiborne of Louisiana, whose nephew J. F. H. Claiborne passed it to the American Naturalist.

heading: English-Chinantec Vocabulary.
short: Observations on the Chinantec Language of Mexico
author: Daniel G. Brinton
place: San Pedro de Yolos (Yolox), Oaxaca, Mexico
title: Observations on the Chinantec Language of Mexico
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 30, 1892, pp. 29-31
about: Brinton compiled this vocabulary from a manuscript copy of Nicolás de la Barreda's Doctrina Christiana en Lengua Chinanteca (Mexico, 1730), written while Barreda was cura of San Pedro de Yolos.

heading: English-Mazatecan Vocabulary.
short: On the Mazatec Language of Mexico
author: Daniel G. Brinton
collector: a Danish officer in the service of Maximilian (manuscript furnished by Alphonse Pinart)
place: Huantla (Huautla), northeast of Teutitlan, Oaxaca, Mexico
title: On the Mazatec Language of Mexico and its Affinities
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 30 (no. 137), 1892, pp. 31-39 (vocabulary pp. 33-35)
about: An unpublished vocabulary collected at Huantla by a Danish officer in the service of Maximilian, furnished to Brinton by Alphonse Pinart.

heading: The following Words and Phrases in the Socotran and Arabic are given as a Specimen of the Language of that Island.
short: Memoir on the Island of Socotra
author: J. R. Wellsted
title: Memoir on the Island of Socotra
imprint: Journal of the Royal Geographical Society of London, 5, 1835, pp. 220-229
about: Printed as a specimen of the language of Socotra, with Arabic and the Socotran words in Arabic script beside them.

heading: List of Kāfir words, compared with those given by Sir A. Burnes.
short: On the Language of the So-called Kafirs of the Indian Caucasus
author: Ernest Trumpp
collector: Ernest Trumpp, from three Kafirs recruited by Major Lumsden at Mardan and sent to Peshawar via Col. Herbert Edwardes, with Muhammad Rasul, a Kuhistani of Panjcore, as interpreter
title: On the Language of the so-called Kafirs of the Indian Caucasus
imprint: Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, 19, 1862, pp. 1-29
about: Trumpp took down the Kafir words at Peshawar from three Kafir men brought from Mardan, with the Panjcore Kuhistani Muhammad Rasul interpreting, and added a short Kuhistani (Kooner) list and Burnes's earlier forms for comparison.

heading: The following words were obtained by the Rev. Mr. Crummell, from a crowd of recaptured Africans, landed at Sino, in Liberia, about two hundred miles west of Cape Palmas.
short: Words from recaptured Africans landed at Sino, Liberia
author: J. P. Lesley (vocabularies obtained by Rev. Alexander Crummell)
title: Stated Meeting, January 3, 1862
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 9, 1862, pp. 3-4
about: Words taken by Alexander Crummell, with the help of interpreters, from about four hundred recaptured Africans landed from a United States war vessel at Sino, Liberia.

heading: Vocabulary of the Onas Language, Tierra del Fuego.
author: D. G. Brinton
title: Further Notes on Fuegian Languages
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 30, 1892, pp. 252-253
about: Brinton reprints the Ona vocabulary that Dr. Polidoro A. Segers printed in the Boletín del Instituto Geográfico Argentino (Buenos Aires, 1891), apparently obtained from the Parrikens band, adding Yahgan and Tsoneca comparisons.

heading: The accompanying Vocabulary was obtained by Mr. Masury, of Salem, Massachusetts, from a native of the Comoro Islands, who had resided several years at Zanzibar.
short: A Vocabulary of the Soahili Language
author: Samuel K. Masury
collector: Samuel K. Masury, from a native of the Comoro Islands
title: A Vocabulary of the Soahili Language, on the Eastern Coast of Africa; by Samuel K. Masury. Communicated by Charles Pickering, M. D.
imprint: Memoirs of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, new series, vol. 2, 1846, pp. 248-252
about: Words and phrases written down at Zanzibar in 1844 by Samuel K. Masury of Salem, Massachusetts, from a native of the Comoro Islands who had lived several years at Zanzibar, and passed to Dr. Charles Pickering.

heading: Limboo Vocabulary. Two Hundred Words. (V. for verb ; N. for noun.)
author: A. Campbell
title: On the Tribes around Darjeeling
imprint: Transactions of the Ethnological Society of London, 7, 1869, pp. 157-159
about: An English–Limbu vocabulary of about two hundred words with numerals, printed by A. Campbell to close his account of the Limboos among the tribes around Darjeeling.

heading: The following is the list of the words sent me. The orthography is German.
author: Daniel G. Brinton
place: Musquito Coast (Rama: small island in Blewfield lagoon; Twaka: headwaters of the Tungla or Princeapula rivers; San Blas words picked up on the coast)
title: Vocabularies from the Musquito Coast
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, XXIX, No. 135, 1891, pp. 1-4
about: Word lists of Rama, Twaka and Cuna (San Blas) sent to Brinton by Rev. W. Siebarger, a United Brethren missionary resident on the Musquito coast, and read before the American Philosophical Society on March 6, 1891.

lang: Jebero, Cholón, Manao, Bonari and others
heading: English-Jivaro Vocabulary; English-Cholona Vocabulary; English-Manao Words; English-Bonari Vocabulary; Descripcion del Indio (Hongote)
short: Studies in South American Native Languages
author: Daniel G. Brinton
place: Upper Marañon (Jivaro/Xebero); upper Huallaga river (Cholona); lower Rio Negro (Manao); river Uatuma (Bonari); east coast of Patagonia (Hongote)
heard: Cholona: 1748 (copy 1772); Jivaro: close of 18th century; Manao: c. 1740; Bonari: before 1874; Hongote: c. 1789
title: Studies in South American Native Languages
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 30 (no. 137), 1892, pp. 65-67, 73-74, 77, 83-85
about: Brinton compiled these word lists from manuscripts in the British Museum and, for Bonari, from Francisco Bernardino de Souza's Para e Amazonas (1874-5).

heading: I obtained lately a manuscript copy of the vocabularies of some languages spoken on the Upper Orinoco and its affluents which had been collected by Mr F. Montolieu, a Frenchman, who for several years acted first as secretary to the governor of the Venezuelan territory Amazonas and was finally governor himself (1870 to 1876).
author: A. Ernst
title: Upper Orinoco Vocabularies
about: Spanish-keyed vocabularies of Yavitero (second half, from L), Puinabo and Piaroa collected by F. Montolieu, a former governor of the Venezuelan territory Amazonas, and published by A. Ernst from a manuscript copy.

heading: In the vocabulary, the words from the list by Noguera are marked with an N. Those not so distinguished are from the article of Mendoza.
short: The Matagalpan Linguistic Stock of Central America
author: D. G. Brinton
heard: Noguera's list after 1853; Mendoza's article published June 1895
title: The Matagalpan Linguistic Stock of Central America
imprint: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society, 34, 1895, pp. 411-414 (vocabulary); article 403-415
about: Brinton combined words from Jeremias Mendoza's 1895 article on Cacaopera in La Universidad (San Salvador) with a list furnished to Berendt by Rev. Victor Noguera, curate at Matagalpa and San Jorge, marking Noguera's words with N.

heading: Vocabularies from Eight Aboriginal Dialects of the Island of Formosa, Collected by J. B. Steere, University of Michigan, during the winter of 1873-74. Six Lists of Words from the Aboriginal Languages of Formosa.
author: J. B. Steere
collector: J. B. Steere; Rev. G. L. Mackay (Onlau); Rev. H. Ritchie (Pilam)
title: Formosa
imprint: Journal of the American Geographical Society of New York, 6, 1874, pp. 302-334 (vocabularies pp. 322-333)
about: J. B. Steere collected six word lists from the Tsui-whan, Lek-whan, Che-whan, Pepo-whan (from old women at Kongana and Bankimseng) and Kale-whan with the help of a Chinese interpreter in 1873-74, adding lists from Onlau and Pilam supplied by the missionaries Makay and Ritchie.
